# Job Chapter 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 418v

---

**1** "Isn't all of human life a struggle?
Our days are like those of a hired laborer —

**2** like a slave longing for the shade at the end of the day,
like a worker waiting to be paid.

**3** I have been given months of futility;
nights of agony have been assigned to me.

**4** When I lie down I think, 'When will morning come?'
But the night stretches on and on, and I toss until dawn.

**5** My body is covered with maggots and scabs;
my skin cracks open and oozes.

**6** My days fly by faster than a weaver's shuttle,
and they end without a shred of hope.

**7** Remember, God — my life is just a breath.
I will never see happiness again.

**8** You see me now, but soon you won't.
You will look for me, but I will be gone.

**9** As a cloud dissolves and disappears,
so the dead go down to the grave and never return.

**10** They never go home again;
their place forgets they ever existed.

**11** So I will not keep quiet.
I will speak out in my anguish;
I will pour out my bitterness.

**12** Am I the sea? Am I a sea monster?
Is that why you post a guard over me?

**13** When I think, 'At least my bed will comfort me,
my couch will ease my suffering,'

**14** you terrorize me with dreams
and horrify me with visions.

**15** I would rather be strangled —
I would rather die than go on living in this body.

**16** I despise my life. I don't want to live forever.
Just leave me alone! My life is nothing but a breath.

**17** What are human beings that you make so much of them,
that you focus your attention on them,

**18** examining them every morning,
testing them every single moment?

**19** Won't you ever look away from me?
Won't you leave me alone long enough to swallow my own spit?

**20** Even if I have sinned, what have I done to you, O Watcher of Humanity?
Why have you made me your target?
Why have I become a burden to myself?

**21** Why won't you just forgive whatever I've done wrong
and let my guilt go?
Soon enough I will lie down in the dust,
and when you come looking for me, I will be gone."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The anti-psalm (vv.17-18):** Job takes one of the most beloved passages in the Psalms — "What is man that you are mindful of him?" (Psalm 8:4) — and turns it into a complaint. In the psalm, God's attention to humanity is a cause for praise. In Job's mouth, it becomes surveillance. This is not blasphemy but the deepest form of engagement with God: he takes the tradition seriously enough to argue with it.

**"Am I the sea?" (v.12):** This is Job's most mythologically rich question. In ancient cosmology, the sea represents primordial chaos that God must restrain. Job asks: am I really that dangerous? Must God guard me as if I were the forces of cosmic destruction? The irony is cutting — a worm-covered man on an ash heap, treated like a cosmic threat.

**"Leave me alone" (v.16,19):** Job's prayer is the inverse of the psalmist's prayer. Where David says "Do not hide your face from me," Job says "Look away." He wants less of God, not more — because divine attention has become identical to suffering.

---
*— PNEUMA*
